options: Is the single joint connecting the lower limb to the trunk
Is frequently dislocated because of its instability
Is a trochlear joint with one axis of movement
Is deep, weight-bearing, mobile and highly congruent
Is a ball-and-socket (spheroid) joint
questions.explanation: The hip is a spheroid joint with three axes; it is very stable, so dislocations are rare.

questions.stem: About the acetabulum as an articular surface of the hip:
options: It is entirely articular
It is bordered by the acetabular limbus
Its peripheral semilunar surface is articular and crescent-shaped
It is located on the medial surface of the hip bone
Its central acetabular fossa is non-articular
questions.explanation: Only the semilunar surface is articular; the acetabulum is on the lateral surface of the hip bone.

options: Is a fibrocartilaginous ring attached to the perimeter of the acetabulum
Increases the depth and extent of the acetabulum
Makes the acetabulum shallower
Is made of hyaline cartilage
Bridges the ischiopubic notch, forming the ligament of the head of the femur
questions.explanation: The labrum is fibrocartilage, not hyaline cartilage. Also false: "Bridges the ischiopubic notch, forming the ligament of the head of the femur"; "Makes the acetabulum shallower".

questions.stem: The capsule of the hip joint inserts:
options: On the acetabular limbus and labrum
On the intertrochanteric line and femoral neck
On the ischial tuberosity
On the greater trochanter's tip
On the fovea capitis
questions.explanation: Iliac insertion: limbus and labrum; femoral insertion: intertrochanteric line and femoral neck.

options: Extends between the acetabulum and the intertrochanteric line
Extends between the ischium and the femoral neck
Is anterior, triangular and strong
Reinforces the posterior part of the capsule
Has two bundles, superior and inferior
questions.explanation: The posterior reinforcement from ischium to femoral neck is the ischiofemoral ligament.

questions.stem: Which ligament of the hip extends between the iliopectineal eminence and the pretrochanteric depression, reinforcing the anteroinferior capsule?
options: The transverse acetabular ligament
The pubofemoral ligament
The iliofemoral ligament
The ischiofemoral ligament
The ligament of the femoral head
questions.explanation: Pubofemoral: iliopectineal eminence → pretrochanteric depression (anteroinferior). Ischiofemoral: posterior; iliofemoral: anterior.

questions.stem: The ligament of the head of the femur (round ligament):
options: Ends by three bundles: anterior horn of the semilunar surface, transverse ligament, ischium
Is intra-synovial and reinforces the capsule
Is extra-articular
Contains an artery supplying the femoral head
Arises from the acetabular fossa and ends on the greater trochanter
questions.explanation: It has its own synovium, independent of the joint synovium, so it is extra-synovial; it does not reinforce the capsule. Also false: "Is extra-articular"; "Arises from the acetabular fossa and ends on the greater trochanter".

questions.stem: After a posterior hip dislocation, the round ligament is torn. What complication can this cause?
options: Rupture of the iliopsoas
Necrosis of the acetabular labrum
Paralysis of the gluteus maximus
Fracture of the iliac crest
Necrosis of the femoral head
questions.explanation: The round ligament carries an artery to the femoral head; its rupture in dislocation risks necrosis of the head.

questions.stem: Match the periarticular muscle group of the hip with its position:
options: Lateral: tensor fasciae latae, gluteus medius, gluteus minimus
Posterior: gluteus maximus, pelvi-trochanteric muscles, hamstrings
Anterior: gluteus maximus
Anterior: iliopsoas, rectus femoris, sartorius
Medial: pectineus, adductor longus, adductor magnus
questions.explanation: Gluteus maximus belongs to the posterior group.

questions.stem: About the synovium of the hip:
options: The round ligament's synovium attaches around the fovea capitis and acetabular fossa
The round ligament's synovium is continuous with the joint synovium
The ligament of the femoral head has its own synovium
It covers the articular cartilage of the femoral head
It lines the deep surface of the capsule
questions.explanation: The synovium of the round ligament is separate and independent from the articular synovium.

options: Flexion reaches 90° with the knee bent
Extension reaches 30° with the knee extended
Extension reaches 20° with the knee extended
Flexion reaches 120° with the knee extended
They occur around a transverse axis through the centre of the femoral head
questions.explanation: Flexion: 120° knee bent, 90° knee extended. Extension: 10° knee bent, 20° knee extended. Also false: "Flexion reaches 90° with the knee bent"; "Extension reaches 30° with the knee extended".

questions.stem: What is the range of hip extension with the knee bent?
questions.explanation: Extension is 10° with the knee bent and 20° with the knee extended.

options: Forced abduction can reach 45° to 60° (gymnastics)
They occur around an anteroposterior axis through the centre of the femoral head
Abduction occurs around a vertical axis
Adduction reaches 60°
Usual abduction is 60°
questions.explanation: Rotations occur around the vertical axis; abduction/adduction around the anteroposterior (sagittal) axis. Also false: "Usual abduction is 60°"; "Adduction reaches 60°".

options: Circumduction results from the succession of the four other movements
Medial rotation has a larger range than lateral rotation
They occur around a vertical axis through the centre of the femoral head
They occur around a transverse axis
Lateral rotation has a larger range than medial rotation
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation (up to 60°) exceeds medial rotation (30°–45°); both occur around the vertical axis.

options: Is screened with the Ortolani manoeuvre
Is treated by swaddling the baby with the hips in forced abduction
Is treated by swaddling with the hips in forced adduction
Is detected at birth
Is screened by measuring the neck–shaft angle
questions.explanation: Ortolani manoeuvre looks for instability; treatment = swaddling in forced abduction.

questions.stem: Which pathologies of the hip are mentioned in the course?
options: Coxarthrosis (osteoarthritis of the hip)
Arthritis (serious inflammation or infection)
Carpal tunnel syndrome
Frequent traumatic dislocations because of instability
Fractures of the femoral neck or acetabulum
questions.explanation: Dislocations are rare because the hip is very stable.
